newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Analysts downbeat on Colombia's '97 GDP growth.
newsitem.headline: Analysts downbeat on Colombia's '97 GDP growth.

text.p: Colombia's leading financial association and the country's top economic think tank jointly forecast the economy would grow by just 2.3 percent this year, compared to the government target of between 3 percent and 3.5 percent.

At a forum in Bogota on macroeconomic performance, the influential National Association of Financial Institutions (ANIF) and independent economic research institute Fedesarrollo forecast zero percent Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth for the first half of this year.
GDP fell by 1.22 percent in the first quarter of 1997.
"The signs of the problem and of recession are still extremely worrying," ANIF chairman Armando Montenegro said.
Fedesarrollo chief Mauricio Cardenas said that despite a slight upturn in the construction and manufacturing industries, investment in capital goods continued to fall.
Cardenas predicted that the main motor for growth this year would be the oil and mining sector, which he said would grow 9.5 percent, compared to the government's forecast of 12 percent.
Montenegro calculated GDP growth would be just 1.5 percent this year if coffee and oil were excluded.
Last year, Colombia's GDP grew 2.08 percent -- one of its lowest growth rates in a decade.

ANIF and Fedesarrollo predicted GDP would increase between 3.5 percent and 3.8 percent in 1998 against the government's aim of about 5 percent. Montenegro said much of that growth would be driven by rising oil output.
